_why: The mutants that SURVIVED and are NOT declared equivalent. There are none, and this file is kept rather than deleted because its four entries are the record of how the score got from 0.852 to 1.000 -- by two rules in the generator, not by four declarations. Each entry below now carries what it was, why it survived, and the measurement that killed it. Units #1 and #4 drew the line this file applies: a survivor no input can distinguish is equivalent, a survivor THIS input set cannot distinguish is a blind spot, and calling the second the first is how a real defect gets excused. All four here were the second kind, and the remedy for the second kind is a corpus, not a paragraph.
_score: 27 killed of 27 behavioural scoreable, 4 declared equivalent, 0 failed to compile, 31 mutants over 8 operators, score 1.000. mutation/ChkParseData.json, taken on the CLEAN tree against the Fortran reference at 1552 cases.

6b46c3dc.site: UCVarNameLen, the declared width of the reference's own CHARACTER(20) locals
6b46c3dc.why_it_survived: It widens the TRUNCATION as well as the buffer. `FndUCVarName = Words(1)` truncates a 200-byte word to 20 bytes, so two parameter names agreeing to character 20 compare EQUAL in the reference and this mutant moves that boundary to 21. Distinguishing it needs a case in which the two names agree to character 20 and differ at 21. R6's length ladder was [1, 2, 6, 11] -- every rung shorter than the boundary -- so no case in that corpus reached a 21st character at all.
6b46c3dc.closed_by: R12_narrowing_width. The width is mined from the reference's own body (vit/checks.py::_narrowing_local transcribed, P4) and the cases set every string parameter from ONE body with a per-parameter mark at index 20.
6b46c3dc.killed: 6 of 1552 -- the same six cases evidence/ChkParseData/harness.no-truncation-stub.json moves, where before it moved 0 of 1284. With R12 ablated (evidence/ChkParseData/mutation.ablate-R12_narrowing_width.json) it survives again at 1540 cases.

d1fc8fa6.why_it_survived: THE SAME GAP. `min(len_src, len_dst)` differs from `len_src` only when `len_src > len_dst`, i.e. only when the source is longer than the 20-byte destination.
d1fc8fa6.closed_by: R12_narrowing_width, at its W+1 and W+5 rungs.
d1fc8fa6.killed: by a CRASH rather than a mismatch, which is what the mutant deserves: 21 bytes are memcpy'd into a 20-byte buffer and the memset that follows is handed (20 - 21) as a size_t. Survives with R12 ablated.

9d9db83a.site: Int2LStrLen, the declared width of Int2LStr's CHARACTER(11) result
9d9db83a.why_it_survived: It moves the READ bound onto a byte nothing writes. The generated Fortran bridge writes exactly 11 bytes (`DO vit_ri_int2lstr = 1, 11`, compiled from the FUNCTION's own declaration and not from this constant), so under the mutant `ftrim(lineNumStr, 12)` reads one byte the program never defined.
9d9db83a.closed_by: R12_narrowing_width, and this one was NOT predicted -- the last dispatch recorded it as a mutant no corpus could kill deterministically, because whether the extra byte reads as a blank is a property of the stack rather than of the input.
9d9db83a.killed: 9 of 1552. THE MECHANISM IS STILL AN INDETERMINATE READ and this entry does not pretend otherwise: what changed is that the corpus now contains inputs under which that byte is not a blank. The attribution is a measurement and not the count: 9 is also exactly the number of R12 cases that reach the message-writing arm, but an equal count is not an equal set (unit #27) -- what settles it is that the mutant dies with R12 in the corpus and SURVIVES with R12 ablated.
9d9db83a.what_was_not_done: The buffer is still not zero-initialised. Zero-initialising it would also kill this mutant and would be defining bytes the correct program never reads, purely to move a number; the same refusal unit #4 made on Conv2UC.

7891029b.site: assign_errmsg's refusal to overrun the staging buffer
7891029b.why_it_survived: The two differ on exactly one input: a message whose length EQUALS the staging buffer's capacity, where the reference-shaped code writes it and the mutant refuses. The capacity was not an input at all -- `emit.ALLOC_HEADROOM` added a constant 4096 to whatever the case supplied, in every case of every corpus this generator has produced, and the messages are ~127 bytes.
7891029b.closed_by: R13_staging_capacity. The capacity now travels in the case stream and R13 sweeps it 0..255 above what the case supplies, with every other input held so the message has ONE length across the block.
7891029b.killed: by EXACTLY 1 of 1552 -- the single case where the capacity equals the 127-byte message. Survives with R13 ablated. The guard was never dead: negating it is killed by a crash.
7891029b.the_boundary_is_now_visible_in_the_run: `VIT: ChkParseData: ErrVar%ErrMsg needs 127 bytes, the staging buffer holds 126; the assignment is refused` -- and the generated Fortran bridge prints its own refusal beside it, which is what makes the two sides agree on the arm rather than merely agree on the outputs.
